subject: CHEMISTRY
caption: Balancing chemical equations, explained in 6 swipes. Save this for your next quiz. Free Chemistry study guide, quizzes, and flashcards at precisstudy.com/chemistry (no sign-up).

slides.title: THE METHOD
lines: Same number of each atom on both sides
slides.note: Count atoms, balance one element at a time, then recount.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
steps: O: 2 on the left, 1 on the right, so put 2 in front of H₂O
H: now 4 on the right, so put 2 in front of H₂

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
steps: O: 2 and 3 → lowest common multiple is 6, so 3O₂ and 2Fe₂O₃
Fe: 4 on the right, so put 4 in front of Fe

slides.title: WATCH OUT
points: Changing a subscript changes the substance: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide, not water.
Only coefficients are yours to change.

pageTitle: How to Balance Chemical Equations in 3 Steps
description: Balance chemical equations with two worked examples and the subscript mistake to avoid.
